disease_label: Rett syndrome (classical, atypical, and RTT-like phenotypes)
source_title: Identification of novel genetic causes of Rett syndrome-like phenotypes
source_journal: Journal of Medical Genetics (J Med Genet 2016;53:190-199)

expected_evidence.value: Rett syndrome (classical, atypical, and RTT-like phenotypes)

partial/complete loss of acquired purposeful hand skills; stereotypical hand movements (hand-wringing/squeezing); partial/complete loss of acquired spoken language; gait abnormalities including ataxic and dyspraxic gait; developmental regression; severe intellectual disability; epilepsy/seizures (including West syndrome in some patients); autistic features / autism spectrum disorder; breathing disturbances (hyperventilation, apnoea, hyperpnoea); bruxism when awake; impaired sleep pattern; scoliosis/kyphosis; growth retardation; small cold hands and feet (peripheral vasomotor disturbances); microcephaly (in some patients); global developmental delay; screaming/crying spells; diminished response to pain
Variable; regression/stagnation reported from ~4-6 months up to ~24 months across patients (no single MECP2-related onset)
